nodeData.topic: Glomerular filtration and clearance in depth
nodeData.note: How the glomerulus filters plasma, how GFR is controlled, measured and estimated, and how it is used to stage CKD. Study aid, reviewed by AI; doctor review in progress — confirm with your lecturer and current guidelines.

children.note: What GFR is and the sieve that makes the filtrate.
GFR is the volume of plasma filtered from all glomerular capillaries into Bowman's space per unit time, usually given in mL/min.

manas.q: What is the glomerular filtration rate?

children.note: Fenestrated capillary endothelium, the glomerular basement membrane, and podocyte foot processes joined by slit diaphragms.

manas.q: Name the three layers of the glomerular filtration barrier.

children.note: Small solutes pass freely; large molecules are held back. Negative charges in the barrier repel anionic proteins such as albumin.

manas.q: Why is albumin normally kept out of the filtrate?

children.note: Filtrate is almost protein-free plasma: water, ions, glucose, amino acids, urea and creatinine at roughly plasma concentrations.

manas.q: What is the composition of glomerular filtrate?

children.note: Pressures that push fluid out of, or pull it back into, glomerular capillaries.
The main force favouring filtration; about 60 mmHg in classic textbook figures, kept high because the efferent arteriole adds resistance downstream.

manas.q: What is the main force driving glomerular filtration?

children.note: Opposes filtration (about 18 mmHg in textbook figures); rises sharply if the urinary tract is obstructed.

manas.q: Which Starling force rises in urinary tract obstruction?

children.note: Plasma protein pull opposing filtration; it rises along the capillary as protein-free fluid leaves, so filtration falls toward the efferent end.

manas.q: Why does oncotic pressure rise along the glomerular capillary?

children.note: Close to zero, because the filtrate contains almost no protein.

manas.q: Why is oncotic pressure in Bowman's space near zero?

children.note: Net pressure = (PGC − PBS) − (πGC − πBS); with textbook figures this is roughly 10 mmHg.

manas.q: How is net filtration pressure across the glomerulus calculated?

children.note: GFR = Kf × net filtration pressure. Kf reflects permeability and surface area; it is very high in glomeruli and falls when glomeruli are lost or scarred.

manas.q: What two factors multiply to give GFR?

children.note: How afferent and efferent tone change GFR and plasma flow.
Lowers glomerular pressure and renal plasma flow, so GFR falls. Afferent dilation does the opposite.

manas.q: What does afferent arteriole constriction do to GFR?

children.note: Raises glomerular pressure so GFR rises modestly, while plasma flow falls; filtration fraction therefore rises.

manas.q: What happens to filtration fraction when the efferent arteriole constricts?

children.note: Low plasma protein lowers oncotic pressure and tends to raise GFR; high plasma protein tends to lower it.

manas.q: How does low plasma protein affect GFR?

children.note: Constricts efferent more than afferent arterioles at low levels, helping preserve GFR when renal perfusion falls.

manas.q: How does angiotensin II help preserve GFR in low perfusion?

children.note: Dilate the afferent arteriole, protecting GFR when perfusion is poor; NSAIDs block this.

manas.q: Which local mediators dilate the afferent arteriole?

children.note: Marked sympathetic activation (e.g. haemorrhage) constricts afferent arterioles and lowers renal blood flow and GFR.

manas.q: What does strong sympathetic activation do to GFR?

children.note: Keeps GFR and renal blood flow steady despite everyday blood pressure changes.
Raised pressure stretches the afferent arteriole wall; smooth muscle contracts in response, limiting the rise in glomerular pressure.

manas.q: How does the myogenic mechanism protect the glomerulus?

children.note: Macula densa cells sense NaCl reaching the end of the thick ascending limb; more NaCl triggers afferent constriction (adenosine is a key mediator), bringing GFR back down.

manas.q: What does the macula densa sense in tubuloglomerular feedback?

children.note: Macula densa, granular (juxtaglomerular) cells that release renin, and extraglomerular mesangial cells, sitting where the distal tubule meets its own glomerulus.

manas.q: What are the parts of the juxtaglomerular apparatus?

children.note: Below the autoregulatory range, GFR falls with blood pressure, so severe hypotension reduces urine output.

manas.q: Why does urine output fall in severe hypotension?

children.note: Turning urine and plasma measurements into kidney function numbers.
The volume of plasma completely cleared of a substance per minute; it is a virtual volume, not a real one.

manas.q: What does renal clearance of a substance represent?

children.note: Urine creatinine 10 mmol/L, plasma 0.1 mmol/L, urine flow 1 mL/min: clearance = (10 × 1) ÷ 0.1 = 100 mL/min.

manas.q: Urine creatinine 10 mmol/L, plasma 0.1 mmol/L, flow 1 mL/min: what is the clearance?

children.note: Filtered load = GFR × plasma concentration of a freely filtered substance; compare it with excretion to see if the tubule reabsorbs or secretes.

manas.q: How do you calculate the filtered load of a substance?

children.note: Equal to GFR: filtered only (inulin). Less than GFR: net reabsorption (urea; glucose normally zero). More than GFR: net secretion (PAH).

manas.q: What does a clearance greater than GFR tell you?

children.note: FF = GFR ÷ renal plasma flow; normally about 20%, so most plasma leaves via the efferent arteriole unfiltered.

manas.q: How is filtration fraction calculated?

children.note: Renal blood flow = renal plasma flow ÷ (1 − haematocrit).

manas.q: How do you convert renal plasma flow to renal blood flow?

children.note: Proximal tubule glucose carriers saturate; above a plasma level of roughly 10 mmol/L glucose spills into urine (glycosuria).

manas.q: Why does glucose appear in urine when plasma glucose is high?

children.note: CH2O = urine flow − osmolar clearance. Positive when urine is dilute, negative when urine is concentrated.

manas.q: What does a positive free water clearance mean?

children.note: Substances used to measure or estimate GFR.
Freely filtered, not reabsorbed, secreted or metabolised by the tubule, not toxic, and easy to measure.

manas.q: List the properties of an ideal GFR marker.

children.note: Exogenous markers such as iohexol or radiolabelled agents (e.g. 51Cr-EDTA, 99mTc-DTPA) measure GFR when an estimate is not reliable enough.

manas.q: Name exogenous markers used to measure GFR.

children.note: Made from muscle creatine at a fairly steady rate; output depends on muscle mass, so sex, age, body build and diet affect serum levels.

manas.q: Why does serum creatinine depend on muscle mass?

children.note: The relation is inverse: halving GFR roughly doubles serum creatinine, so early GFR loss may leave creatinine within the normal range.

manas.q: Why can serum creatinine stay normal despite early loss of GFR?

children.note: Trimethoprim, cimetidine and dolutegravir reduce tubular creatinine secretion, raising serum creatinine slightly without a true fall in GFR.

manas.q: Which drugs raise serum creatinine without lowering true GFR?

children.note: A small protein made by all nucleated cells; less affected by muscle mass than creatinine, but influenced by thyroid status, steroids and inflammation.

manas.q: Why is cystatin C useful when muscle mass is unusual?

children.note: Poor GFR marker: partly reabsorbed and changed by protein intake, GI bleeding, catabolism and dehydration.

manas.q: Why is urea a poor marker of GFR?

children.note: Measures creatinine clearance from a timed urine collection; incomplete collections are a common source of error.

manas.q: What is the main pitfall of 24-hour urine creatinine clearance?

children.note: Formulas that estimate GFR from blood markers and patient factors.
Estimates creatinine clearance (mL/min) from age, weight, sex and serum creatinine; not indexed to body surface area.

manas.q: Which variables does the Cockcroft–Gault equation use?

children.note: Estimate GFR indexed to 1.73 m² body surface area; CKD-EPI is more accurate than MDRD at higher GFR values.

manas.q: What body surface area are MDRD and CKD-EPI results indexed to?

children.note: eGFR assumes stable creatinine; in acute kidney injury creatinine lags behind the real change, so eGFR misleads.

manas.q: Why is eGFR unreliable in acute kidney injury?

children.note: Less reliable at extremes of muscle mass or body size, after amputation, and in pregnancy.

manas.q: Name situations where creatinine-based eGFR is less reliable.

children.note: Staging chronic kidney disease by GFR and albuminuria.
Abnormal kidney structure or function lasting more than 3 months, with implications for health.

manas.q: How long must kidney abnormalities last to define CKD?
Give the GFR range for CKD stage G3b.

children.note: With GFR ≥60, CKD needs another marker of damage, such as albuminuria or structural change.

manas.q: What is needed to diagnose CKD when GFR is above 60?

children.note: By urine albumin:creatinine ratio: A1 <3, A2 3–30, A3 >30 mg/mmol.

manas.q: What albumin:creatinine ratio defines albuminuria category A3?

children.note: Where GFR physiology meets the ward.
Low renal perfusion (e.g. dehydration, haemorrhage) lowers GFR; at first the tubules still work and the change can reverse with restored perfusion.

manas.q: Why does GFR fall in dehydration or haemorrhage?

children.topic: ACE inhibitors and renal artery stenosis
children.note: With bilateral renal artery stenosis, GFR depends on angiotensin II efferent tone; ACE inhibitors can then cause a sharp fall in GFR.

manas.q: Why can ACE inhibitors drop GFR in bilateral renal artery stenosis?

children.note: Many renally cleared drugs need dose changes when GFR is low; check the drug's prescribing guidance.

manas.q: Why must renal function be checked before prescribing some drugs?

children.note: GFR rises by about 50% in normal pregnancy, so serum creatinine is normally lower than outside pregnancy.

manas.q: What happens to GFR in normal pregnancy?

children.note: Early diabetes can raise GFR above normal (hyperfiltration) before later decline; albuminuria is an early sign of diabetic kidney disease.

manas.q: What happens to GFR early in diabetic kidney disease?

children.note: GFR tends to fall with age, while low muscle mass in older people can hide this behind a normal creatinine.

manas.q: Why may older people have a normal creatinine despite low GFR?

children.note: How eGFR is reported and used in different places.
International KDIGO guidance stages CKD by cause, GFR category and albuminuria category together.

manas.q: Which three elements does KDIGO use to classify CKD?

children.note: The US NKF–ASN task force (2021) recommended the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation and wider use of cystatin C.

manas.q: Which eGFR equation did the US task force recommend in 2021?

children.note: The European Kidney Function Consortium equation is designed to work across ages from children to older adults, with creatinine or cystatin C.

manas.q: What is the EKFC equation?

children.note: Papers read 2026-11-20.
A 2024 review covers how creatinine and cystatin C are measured, their pros and cons, age-related reference ranges and their use in eGFR equations, focusing on EKFC.

manas.q: Which two serum markers are most used to calculate eGFR?

children.note: After an NKF–ASN task force reviewed over 20 approaches, it backed the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation and more cystatin C testing; authors say this aids equity.

manas.q: What did the NKF–ASN task force recommend for eGFR?

children.note: A meta-analysis of 12 studies found race-corrected and creatinine-based equations tended to overestimate GFR in Black people; cystatin C-only equations showed small bias.

manas.q: Which eGFR equations tended to overestimate GFR in Black populations?

children.note: Quick wins.
Afferent constriction: GFR and flow both fall. Efferent constriction: GFR up, flow down, filtration fraction up.

manas.q: Contrast the effects of afferent and efferent constriction on GFR.

children.note: Glucose (≈0) < urea < inulin (= GFR) < PAH (≈ renal plasma flow).

manas.q: Rank glucose, urea, inulin and PAH by clearance.

children.note: Because some creatinine is secreted, its clearance runs slightly above true GFR.

manas.q: Why does creatinine clearance overestimate GFR?

children.note: Back-pressure raises Bowman's space pressure and opposes filtration.

manas.q: How does ureteric obstruction reduce GFR?
